SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - JULY 17, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
SIERRA ROOM - CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING ARTS
18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Sierra Room.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY, JULY
17, 2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE SIERRA ROOM AT CERRITOS CENTER FOR THE PERFORMING
ARTS, 18000 PARK PLAZA DRIVE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Dustin T. Parker, Concordia Lutheran Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Strikers – Cerritos Youth Soccer Team (Elementary
  Division).

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  None.

5B.  Presentation of Cerritos Auto Square Documentary video.

  This item was introduced by Mayor Barrows.

  The Cerritos Auto Square Documentary video by Todd Huffman, Pipeline Digital Media, LLC,
  was played at this time.

5C.  Review and consideration of appointments, removals, and filling of scheduled or unscheduled
  vacancies on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (2022-24 term) (COUNCIL).

  There were no public comments received on this item and no action was taken.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Case van der Linden expressed concerns regarding future plans for the shopping center
  located on the southwest side of South Street and Bloomfield Avenue.

  (minutes continue on the next page)

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence submitted by the deadline listed on the agenda is considered
  public record. Prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency received copies of the full-text
  unredacted written correspondence which was submitted for this item. Public requests for
  copies of the full-text redacted written correspondence can be made during regular
  business hours to the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer).

  Coleen Aldrich submitted comments expressing concern regarding coyote sightings in
  Cerritos.

  Gail Grossman submitted comments expressing concern regarding coyote sightings in
  Cerritos.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Thursday, June 22, 2023, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the Thursday,
  June 22, 2023, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated July 17, 2023 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  July 17, 2023  $ 6,812,382.20 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  (minutes continue on the next page)

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports

  City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer's Reports for the period ending May 31, 2023
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending May 31, 2023
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Approval of annual enterprise and records management system support and maintenance
  agreements for Fiscal Year 2023-24 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the annual
  support and maintenance agreement purchase orders as follows:

  1.  Carahsoft for the Granicus system in the amount of $53,617.58; and

  2.  Iron Mountain for Citywide offsite storage of records, information, and historical data,
  in the amount of $60,000.00 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of contract for construction of tree improvements in
  residential streets,  Project  No.  14088,  Bid  No.  1496-23*  (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines,
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  Agenda Items 9A and 9B were considered concurrently pursuant to City Council Consensus.

  A staff report was given by Amandeep Mann, Associate Civil Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, July 17, 2023, 7:00 p.m.

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public
  Resources Code Section 21000 et seq. (CEQA) that the improvements planned under
  the proposed contract award are categorically exempt pursuant to Section 15301 of the
  CEQA Guidelines, based on the findings as set forth in the agenda report associated
  with this item;

  2. Award a contract in the amount of $115,400.00 for the complete removal of 76
  parkway trees and planting of 64 trees (total bid), to Golden West Arbor Services, Bid
  No. 1496-23, and reject the other bids; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any project-related change orders,
  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of award of contract for construction of concrete improvements in
  residential streets, Project No. 14088, Bid No. 1495-23* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines,
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.

  Agenda Items 9A and 9B were considered concurrently pursuant to City Council Consensus.

  A staff report was given by Amandeep Mann, Associate Civil Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public
  Resources Code Section 21000 et seq. (CEQA) that the improvements planned under
  the proposed contract award are categorically exempt pursuant to Section 15301 of the
  CEQA Guidelines, based on the findings as set forth in the agenda report associated
  with this item;

  2. Award a contract in the amount of $674,000.00 for concrete improvements in
  residential streets (total bid) to CJ Concrete Construction, Inc., Bid No. 1495-23, and
  reject the other bids; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any project-related change orders,
  in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy (COUNCIL).

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal

  None.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Johnson, Vo, Mayor Pro Tem Solanki, and Mayor

12.  Closed Session

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session to

  12E.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Clerk/Treasurer

  The City Council recessed to Closed Session.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT:

  The City Council reconvened into Open Session. Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, reported the City
  Council convened into Closed Session to discuss Items 12A and 12B only, as listed on the
  Closed Session agenda. The City Council received briefings on Items 12A and 12B and no
  reportable action was taken. The City Council did not call up Closed Session Items 12C,
  12D, or 12E (City Manager, City Attorney and City Clerk/Treasurer performance
  evaluations) for discussion.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 9:59 p.m.
